Hm, I haven't explained yet why I thought about the s/g lists. Think of a network packet that is stored across a page boundary. It might be virtually contiguous, but not physically.
For some network cards like rtl8139 you'd need to allocate a physically contiguous buffer and copy the packet there
Other networks cards (I think e1000 is among them) can gather a packet together from chunks in multiple physical buffers
Right, that's what I thought you meant
So if we had a s/g list we can avoid the copy for e1000
